problem_statement: nuxt-ui-templates portfolio is a runnable Nuxt 4 personal portfolio built on @nuxt/ui and @nuxt/content, with a Home page, a Projects page, a Blog, a Speaking page and an About page, all wrapped by a single shared layout (app/layouts/default.vue) that renders the floating navigation header and the footer on every route. This task adds an on-brand 'Availability & focus' rail (a shared FocusRail component, app/components/FocusRail.vue) mounted by that shared layout so the same engagement signals follow the visitor across every page. The rail is a card headed 'Open to new work' with a segmented mode selector of three engagement modes (Consulting, Full-time, Advising) and a four-tile metric row reporting the owner's current working signals (status, response time, focus area, time zone); selecting a mode swaps in a short live readout with no remote request. The rail is authored identically in every evaluation leg (same markup, same copy, same modes and tiles). The delivered reference rail is on-brand (a light white surface with slate text and the blue accent that matches the Nuxt UI portfolio), it is mounted on Home, Projects, Blog, Speaking and About, its four-tile metric row wraps fluidly so the document fits a 390px phone, and its readout is a live computed value that re-derives from the selected mode. Deliver the FocusRail rail so that: (D6) the metric row wraps and no tile is pinned to a rigid width wider than a phone, so the mobile home states report zero horizontal overflow; (D2) the rail is rendered by the shared layout on Home, Projects, Blog, Speaking and About so it follows the visitor across pages; (D3) the rail uses the light on-brand palette (white surface, slate/blue type) matching the portfolio rather than an off-brand dark scheme; and (D4) selecting a mode updates the readout live to reflect the newly selected mode. Preserve the shared navigation header, the footer, the hero, the Projects, Blog, Speaking and About pages, the desktop and tablet layouts, and the visual system; introduce no console or network errors on the covered states. (Note: this Nuxt project builds statically with 'nuxt generate' and the prerendered .output/public is served behind a static file server; that build/serve invocation, together with the offline-buildable configuration and locally-vendored imagery, is supplied as infrastructure in all evaluation legs and is not part of the change.)
required_content: Add the shared 'Availability & focus' FocusRail rail (app/components/FocusRail.vue): a card headed 'Open to new work' with three engagement modes (Consulting, Full-time, Advising) and a four-tile metric row (status, response, focus area, time zone) plus a live readout.
Mount the rail from the shared layout (app/layouts/default.vue) on Home, Projects, Blog, Speaking and About so the availability signals follow the visitor across every page (cross-page presence).

Make the metric row responsive: on the mobile home states the document width must equal the viewport width (no horizontal scrollbar) within the overflow tolerance, by letting the tiles wrap and dropping any rigid per-tile width wider than a phone viewport.
Style the rail on-brand: a light white surface with slate text and the blue accent matching the Nuxt UI portfolio, not an off-brand dark palette, so it is visually consistent with the site.

Wire the mode selector locally with no remote call: selecting a mode updates the live readout to reflect the newly selected engagement mode. The readout reads '<Mode> · <cadence>' (Consulting · This quarter by default); selecting Advising re-derives it to read exactly 'Advising · Ongoing'.

Preserve the shared navigation header, the footer, the hero, the Projects, Blog, Speaking and About pages, the desktop and tablet layouts, and the visual system; introduce no new console or network errors on the covered states.
design_constraints: Keep the site structure: the shared floating navigation header with its links, the footer, the home hero, and the Projects, Blog, Speaking and About pages.

Mount the FocusRail rail from the shared layout so it renders on Home, Projects, Blog, Speaking and About with its heading 'Open to new work', its three engagement modes and its four metric tiles; keep the rail markup and copy identical across legs.
Fix the mobile overflow only by letting the metric row wrap and removing any rigid fixed tile width; do not delete the rail, the metric row or any tile.
Keep the mode-selector interaction working entirely on-page with no remote request, so the covered states stay free of console and network errors.
Preserve the visual system (light surface, blue accent, typography) across desktop, tablet and mobile, and keep the rail on-brand rather than an off-brand dark scheme.
state_constraints: mobile_initial verifies the home page with the FocusRail rail renders within the 390px viewport with no horizontal overflow once the metric row wraps.
desktop_initial verifies the rail, its heading 'Open to new work', its three modes and four metric tiles render on-brand (light surface) with zero overflow.
desktop_projects and desktop_about verify the rail follows the visitor to the secondary pages (cross-page presence) with the shared navigation intact.
desktop_blog and desktop_speaking verify the rail is also present on the Blog and Speaking pages.
mobile_projects verifies the Projects page with the rail fits the mobile viewport.
tablet_initial verifies the tablet layout keeps the rail within the viewport with no horizontal scroll.
desktop_home_advising verifies the mode-selector interaction: selecting the Advising mode updates the live readout to reflect that mode, with no console or network errors.

change_completion: The FocusRail rail is present with its heading 'Open to new work', all three engagement modes and the four metric tiles (status, response, focus area, time zone).
Selecting a mode updates the live readout to reflect the newly selected mode (on-page, no remote request).

The rail reuses the light on-brand palette (white surface, slate text, blue accent) and typography of the portfolio rather than an off-brand dark scheme.
regression: The shared navigation header, footer, hero, and the Projects, Blog, Speaking and About pages remain intact.
No console errors or failed network requests are introduced on the covered states.
responsive: The mobile home states render the rail's metric row within the viewport with no horizontal scroll.
The desktop and tablet layouts remain coherent and unchanged.

author_notes: L4 add task on the nuxt-ui-templates portfolio (Nuxt 4 + @nuxt/ui + @nuxt/content). A shared, on-brand 'Availability & focus' rail (FocusRail component) is mounted by the shared layout app/layouts/default.vue so the same engagement signals follow the visitor across Home, Projects, Blog, Speaking and About. The rail is a card headed 'Open to new work' with three engagement modes (Consulting / Full-time / Advising) and a four-tile metric row (status, response, focus area, time zone); a small client handler updates a live readout when a mode is selected, so there is NO remote request and the covered states stay network-clean. The rail markup and copy are authored identically in all three legs; the two leg-varying files are app/components/FocusRail.vue (rail palette + metric-row layout + readout wiring) and app/layouts/default.vue (which routes the rail is mounted on). The rail carries FOUR orthogonal, independently graded defects. D6 no_horizontal_overflow: the baseline pins the four metric tiles in a fixed-width non-wrapping row (min-width/width 760px), so on a 390px phone the document is forced about 415px wider than the viewport; the reference lets the tiles wrap (flex 1 1 180px, width:auto) so mobile overflow is 0; desktop (1440) and tablet (834) fit either way. D3 visual_regression: the baseline paints the rail in an off-brand dark-teal palette (#0f2c2e surface) that clashes with the light portfolio, so pixelmatch, ssim and block_fidelity over the rail crops on desktop_initial and mobile_initial all fail against the reference's white on-brand surface. D2 dom_assertions: the reference mounts the rail on Home, Projects, Blog, Speaking and About, while the baseline mounts it on Home only, so the .focus-rail class_contains and 'Open to new work' text_contains assertions on the secondary pages fail. D4 interaction_assertions: the reference readout is a Vue computed that re-derives from the active mode; the click that selects the 'Advising' mode updates the readout to 'Advising - Ongoing'. The baseline readout is ALSO a live computed (its D4 wiring is correct), so the baseline PASSES D4 and is leg-orthogonal to the layout/palette/overflow defects. The bad solution is a 'smart wrong' rebuild that fails ALL FOUR orthogonal gates at once: it keeps the off-brand dark palette (D3), pins the tiles in a fixed-min-width non-wrapping row so mobile still overflows about 391px (D6), mounts the rail on Home only so the secondary pages have no rail (D2), AND snapshots the readout once into a plain ref instead of a computed (D4) so clicking 'Advising' moves the active-mode highlight but the readout stays frozen on 'Consulting - This quarter'. The bad click trajectory succeeds (the action is a real interaction), but the terminal readout state is stale, so interaction_assertions fails on the changed_from delta. Content, rail markup and copy are identical across all three legs; the discriminators are the four orthogonal gates. The reference is runtime-clean: zero disallowed console errors and zero failed network requests across all nine covered states, zero horizontal overflow on desktop, tablet and mobile. As declared infrastructure identical in all legs (NOT the change): the upstream template pulls hero, project, blog and avatar imagery from remote unsplash and pexels URLs and downloads Google Fonts at build; for a deterministic, network-free static capture those remote images were revendored to local /img/*.avif assets bundled in public/, the fonts are self-hosted by the build, and the prerendered .output/public is served behind a static file server that serves the @nuxt/content sqlite .wasm asset with the correct application/wasm MIME type. This offline configuration is byte-identical across the reference, baseline and bad legs and is not part of the task diff. Design keywords: availability rail, engagement modes, metric tiles, on-brand palette, responsive layout, cross-page presence, live readout.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: nuxt-ui-templates portfolio (Nuxt 4 + @nuxt/ui + @nuxt/content multi-page personal portfolio) is a runnable, statically generable long-tail-framework website assigned to slot_145 in the 400-task ledger for task_id dev_nuxt-ui-templates__portfolio__265fa1c11e91__availability_focus_rail (intent extend_interaction, capability Edit, scope component). Its single shared layout renders the navigation header and footer on every route, which makes it a clean host for an on-brand shared 'Availability & focus' rail (FocusRail) that follows the visitor across Home, Projects, Blog, Speaking and About. The rail carries four orthogonal, independently graded defects: a mobile horizontal-overflow defect (a fixed-width non-wrapping metric row), an off-brand dark palette that clashes with the light portfolio, a cross-page presence defect (mounted on Home only), and a frozen readout that never re-derives after a mode is selected. The reference repairs all four; the original-with-defect baseline fails overflow, visual-regression and cross-page presence but keeps a correct live readout (passes the interaction gate); the shallow bad rebuild fails all four gates.
